analysis: Supplied changes are documentation only. changelog.d/large-memory-checkpoint-stage-cap.md head:3-9 and docs/reference/configuration.md head:508 describe raising complete-checkpoint default read caps from 1 GiB/1000 ms to 3 GiB/2500 ms on Macs with >=96 GiB; explicit overrides remain authoritative and attention defaults/write budget reportedly remain unchanged. The configuration date also changes at head:3. Reviewed all supplied metadata, patches and surrounding excerpts against the indexed model and full supplied T-041. Larger restores affect transient resource exposure and the existing same-account TTFT oracle (T-041, A-001, TB-007), but these documentation changes establish no concrete security regression or material new threat-model gap. No supplied change modifies authorization, account scoping, encryption, TTL, key custody or billing. Runtime implementation is absent: next pass must inspect SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift cap selection and complete-checkpoint callers, including estimated-read enforcement, native destination/scratch reservations, concurrent restore accounting, cancellation and release/fallback paths. Verify that higher payload caps cannot bypass GlobalKVCacheBudget or cause allocations before reservation, and that authentication/context binding and coordinator-authored cacheSalt remain intact. Documentation assertions are not implementation evidence; unchanged callers were not examined.
